## Clinical Trials

Clinical trials are research studies that investigate new treatments or new ways of using existing treatments. They are necessary to advance the field of veterinary oncology and develop more effective and safer cancer treatments.

At The Cancer Vet, we offer participation in clinical trials, providing your pet with access to innovative treatments that may not be available elsewhere. Our team follows rigorous protocols to ensure the safety and well-being of your pet throughout the trial.

You can leverage our clinical trials by discussing with our team whether your pet is a suitable candidate for any ongoing trials. Participation in a clinical trial can provide your pet with access to cutting-edge treatments and contribute to the advancement of veterinary oncology.

 The Cancer Vet passionately delivers specialized comprehensive cancer care for pets, aiming to enhance their quality of life.

### Project Details

Funding Body: Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH), Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

Project Title: “Anticancer Activity of Combined Homeopathic Preparation of Thuja occidentalis and Carbolic Acid against Canine Mammary Tumour through In Vitro and In Vivo Model”

Operating Department: Department of Veterinary Biochemistry, CVSc&AH, OUAT, Bhubaneswar

Principal Investigator: Pravas Ranjan Sahoo, Department of Veterinary Biochemistry, CVSc&AH, OUAT, Bhubaneswar

### Job Description

Duties and Responsibilities:

  * Laboratory work
  * Field visits
  * Project-related office assistance

### Eligibility Criteria

Essential Qualification:

  * A postgraduate degree (M.Sc) in Basic/Life Science, preferably Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Zoology, Microbiology or Bioinformatics, with minimum 55% marks; or
  * A Master in Veterinary Science (M.V.Sc) with specialisation in Animal Biochemistry, Animal Biotechnology, Veterinary Microbiology or Animal Physiology.

Experience: No prior work experience is listed as essential (Freshers eligible).

### Required Skills

Desirable:

  * NET/GATE/CSIR-UGC qualified candidates will be given preference.
  * Knowledge of basic molecular and analytical techniques, cell culture, gene and protein expression and cancer biology.
  * Knowledge of basic computer operation.

### Salary

Rs 37,000 (consolidated) per month plus HRA as per rules in the first and second year.

Rs 42,000 (consolidated) per month plus HRA as per rules in the third year.

  * No TA/DA will be paid.

When discussing the possibility of participating in a clinical trial with pet owners, it is helpful to share that although “experimental,” or “investigational,” the safety and efficacy of new therapies and procedures have often been evaluated first in laboratory animals as well as normal dogs or cats, and the therapy is considered to be of potential benefit to the patient.

# Clinical Trials

### Welcome to a resource for information on current research trials in veterinary oncology.

Pet owners often ask us if we are aware of any CLINICAL TRIALS that may be available to their cat or dog who has been diagnosed with cancer. While there certainly are a number of studies occurring around the world, participation in a clinical trial can often be difficult, especially if the trial is going on in a hospital or clinic far away from your home.

Each clinical trial has very specific qualifications for participation that include everything from the breed and age of the participant to the life expectancy, weight and of course the type of cancer. Each study is very particular in its criteria for participation. Something else to take into consideration is that clinical trials are NOT always free. There may be fees to participate because grants may only cover a certain portion of the trial, and you may have to travel a long way to participate for several weeks or months perhaps.

The following links represent an organized effort to provide general practitioners and their pet owners access to information to trials being conducted across the United States and, in some cases, in other countries.
